rappel_detail.pull: Double ropes the whole way. Rappelling this way works, but stuck ropes are a known risk; pull steadily.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 1 of about 10, on double ropes, off the summit block toward the north arete and the rock trough at the head of the couloir.
hazards: There is nothing fixed to inspect here — the anchor is whatever you can build out of what is stacked on the summit
rappel_detail.station: Comes straight off the summit block, rigged around a stack of blocks rather than any fixed gear.

rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 2 of about 10, into the upper couloir. Where the flanking rock gives out, at least one party rappelled off a buried deadman picket.
hazards: This face sheds rock steadily and the couloir is the funnel it all comes down — anchoring on the flanking wall keeps you and the ropes out of the middle of it
rappel_detail.station: Into the upper couloir. The anchors are on the rock walls flanking the couloir rather than in the ice — that is where the first ascent placed pins on the way down, and where later parties still rig. Where the flanking rock gives out, at least one party rappelled off a buried picket.

rappel_detail.anchor: slung horn, pin or gear anchor on the flanking rock wall
rappel_detail.station: On the rock wall flanking the couloir, not in the ice: that is where the first ascent placed pins on the way down and where later parties still rig. Expect to build or back up the anchor with slings on horns or your own gear rather than trusting old fixed pins.
rappel_detail.notes: Rappel 3 of about 10, down the north-side couloir on double ropes.

Rappel 10 of about 10, reaching the snow and the bergschrund at the foot of the couloir. Parties often stop rappelling earlier and downclimb the lower couloir when the snow allows.
hazards: The bergschrund at the foot of the north-face couloir still has to be crossed to reach the glacier, and it is the last thing you deal with after a long technical descent
rappel_detail.station: The rappels do not necessarily reach the bottom. Parties commonly stop rappelling partway and downclimb the rest of the couloir, frequently in the dark.

set.rappels: About 10 double-rope rappels down the north-side couloir back to the bergschrund, anchored on the rock walls flanking the couloir; sometimes more, or fewer where the lower couloir can be downclimbed.
set.rappel_count_note: About ten double-rope rappels from the summit to the glacier, with anchors built on the rock walls flanking the couloir. Parties describe ten or more; the count drops when the lower couloir is in condition to downclimb. Rappel lengths are not published station by station.
